notes: The workflow plugin carries no specialists of its own -- it ships skills, scripts and session hooks, so its extensions array is empty by construction rather than unfilled. This repo consumes itself (see CLAUDE.md); through the github source it sees the most recently pushed version, not ongoing branch work. Inventory brought to 19 on 2026-07-29 -- the full roster, matching the enabled plugin exactly. Six were added: 02-09, 03-02, 04-11, 04-12, 04-13, 06-30, whose lenses landed with the adopt-the-six change (PR #212) while this register was not updated alongside. That gap is why an inventory drift can sit unnoticed in the register of the very repo that owns the check: 'exists in the consumer but is not in the register' is an [INFO], and the session hook reports only [ERROR] lines, so nothing surfaced it at session start. It took a deliberate run of check-connectors.ps1 to find. Whoever lands lenses here updates this array in the same change. CAUGHT UP 2026-09-05 (#1465): the workflow plugin's id moved from 'contributing-davekjohn@' to 'dkj-policy@' (source issue #1437, commit 17149edb) and this record held the retired name. Measured in this checkout rather than taken from the report: .claude/settings.json enables dkj-policy@claude-code-specialists, and installed_plugins.json carries a project-scope record for THIS checkout under that id (4.30.0, commit ba889a81) and none at all under the retired one. The empty extensions array is unchanged and is still the measured answer, not an unfilled one: plugins/workflows/dkj-policy/ ships no agents/ (its folder holds blueprint/, hooks/, scripts/, skills/, templates/ and the portable docs). WHAT THE RETIRED NAME COST HERE is precisely what connectors/xoxowildhearts.json recorded for the #886 rename: check-connectors reports an id the marketplace no longer declares as an [INFO] and then SKIPS the whole plugin block, so for this repo's own entry nothing about the workflow plugin was version-checked -- not enabled-in-settings, not extensions, not the machine version. 'The class was never emptied, only its instance was' held a second time: #1437 re-opened the same blind spot by the identical route, and it did so in the register of the repo that OWNS the check. The [INFO] deliberately stays an [INFO] -- making it an error re-opens the four false alarms of August 9, 2026 -- so a consumer catching up IS the repair, and it is the consumer's move rather than the check's. The five other manifests still naming contributing-davekjohn@ are left standing and are correct as they are: the register records what a consumer HAS, and each catches up when it migrates. The sentences above keep the names they were WRITTEN with, per #952. ONE STALE COUNT WAS DROPPED from the opening sentence in the same change: it said 'two session hooks' where the plugin ships five SessionStart hooks and one Stop hook. It is not restated as a number -- that same count went stale twice inside two days on CLAUDE.md's own roster page, which is why that page stopped listing the set at all, and each plugin's hooks/hooks.json is the one place that cannot go stale. CAUGHT UP 2026-09-06 (#1525): the core team's id moved from 'team-alpha@' to 'dkj-team-alpha@' and this record held the retired name -- the OTHER half of the very file the entry above repaired. Measured in this checkout rather than taken from the report: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json declares 'dkj-team-alpha' and no 'team-alpha'; .claude/settings.json at HEAD enables dkj-team-alpha@claude-code-specialists; and installed_plugins.json carries a project-scope record for THIS checkout under that id (4.31.0, commit 5958e52e) beside a stale pre-migration one under the retired id (4.30.0, commit ba889a81). The 19 extensions were RE-READ rather than carried over, because a skipped block had never verified them: the plugin owns exactly 19 ids (15 in agents/, 4 in personas/) and .claude/specialists/lenses/ holds a lens for each, so the array is the measured answer and is unchanged. WHAT THE RETIRED NAME COST HERE is the same skipped block described above, now for the core team: enabled-in-settings, the 19 extensions and the machine version were none of them checked. THE SHARPER HALF IS THE INVERSION. The [INFO] said this repo 'has not migrated to the current names yet' and that the record was 'Correct as it stands' -- both false in the same checkout the script was reading, because settings.json proves the migration two directories away. A doctrine written for a consumer that has NOT moved reads as absolution for one that HAS, so this entry could sit wrong indefinitely while its own check called it right. 'The class was never emptied, only its instance was' therefore held a THIRD time, and this time inside the commit that wrote the sentence: 011a32ef (#1465) changed the workflow plugin's id and left the core team's standing, one block above it. The lesson recorded here is that a rename is checked against EVERY id in a manifest, not against the id the report happened to name. The check is unchanged and the [INFO] deliberately stays an [INFO], for the reason given above; the other manifests naming retired ids are left standing and are still correct as they are, because those consumers have not migrated. The sentences above keep the names they were WRITTEN with, per #952.
